blocking.section: Decision outcome (Transport and Membership rows, Figure 1)
blocking.issue: The ADR treats port 8092 as one peer-certificate-only Raft transport, which contradicts its owning document. Control plane and GitOps, Replica roles 4, makes 8092 a peer layer that authorizes classes by certificate role: Raft and write forwarding for members; status forwarding and content replication for replicas; content fetch and the relay feed for `relay`-role certificates; and a token `Join`. Its Certificates and replica join section says `ruralz control join` redeems a one-time `admin` token in `Join` before the joining replica has any peer certificate. The ADR contradicts this in three places. The Transport row admits 'Ruralz Control peer certificates only'. The Membership row has `ruralz control join` add a voter over that same port. Figure 1 sends content replication through the node that the Transport row reserves for `raft.NetworkTransport`, and it omits the forwarding, relay-feed and Join classes.
blocking.evidence: Line 49: "`raft.NetworkTransport` over a Ruralz mutual-TLS stream layer on `crypto/tls`, never the built-in TCP layer, on 8092 (...); Ruralz Control peer certificates only, Node certificates rejected (TB-11)" / line 51: "`ruralz control join` adds a voter over 8092" / lines 71, 84-85: "tls[\"Mutual-TLS stream layer on 8092\"]", "cas --> tls", "tls -.->|\"Raft and content replication\"| peers" / owning document, Replica roles 4: "8092 authorizes classes by certificate role ... and a token `Join` (OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-15)" / owning document, Certificates and replica join: "`ruralz control join` redeems a one-time `admin` token in `Join`, and the leader signs the replica's certificate and adds a voter"
blocking.fix: Transport row: "A Ruralz mutual-TLS stream layer on `crypto/tls` on 8092, never the built-in TCP layer ([Control Store transport](...)), hands Raft-class connections from voter peer certificates to `raft.NetworkTransport`. The other classes (forwarding, content, relay feed and a token `Join`) follow [Replica roles](../architecture/04-control-plane-and-gitops.md#replica-roles) (OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-15). Node certificates are always rejected (TB-11)." Membership row: "`ruralz control join` redeems a one-time `admin` token in `Join` on 8092; the leader signs the peer certificate and adds a voter". Figure 1: rename `tls` to "Peer layer 8092: classes by certificate role", add an edge `raft --> tls` labeled "Raft class", and relabel the peers edge "Raft, forwarding, content and relay classes". The body is at 1,481 of 1,500 words, so keep the net change within the band. For example, drop the ALPN clause from the Proposed amendments bullet, because OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-15 is now cited in the row.

blocking.issue: The `postgres` row states content placement as decided, which contradicts binding foundation pack section 2. Section 2 defines the Control Store, `postgres` included, as metadata 'plus digest-addressed Revision content and audit segments on Ruralz Control replicas'. The owning document leaves content placement and status forwarding under `postgres` open as OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-22, whose proposed option (a) would amend pack section 2, and whose option (b) is '8092 without Raft'. The row states 'Everything in PostgreSQL' and '8092 is unused' as rules and does not mark either as pending. OQ-22 appears only in More information. Under pack section 14, a deviation from the pack stays an Open question until it is decided.
blocking.evidence: Line 54: "Everything in PostgreSQL over TLS; leadership is a fenced lease row renewed every 2 s and expiring after 10 s (target); sequence checks run in a transaction; 8092 is unused; switching implementations opens a new `storeEpoch`" / foundation pack section 2 Control Store row: "plus digest-addressed Revision content and audit segments on Ruralz Control replicas" / owning document Open questions: "OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-22 | Status forwarding and content placement under `postgres`, amending pack section 2? | (a) PostgreSQL tables (proposed); (b) 8092 without Raft"
blocking.fix: Replace the start of the row with: "Metadata in PostgreSQL over TLS; content placement and status forwarding stay OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-22 (proposed: PostgreSQL tables, amending pack section 2), and 8092 stays unused (pack section 8.4) unless that question picks option (b); ...". Keep the lease, transaction and `storeEpoch` clauses. To stay within 1,500 words, shorten the More information entry to "OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-22" without its parenthetical.

non_blocking.suggestion: The bullet cites System overview TB-11, and TB-11 says 'Quorum loss stops writes only'. Reword it as "quorum loss stops writes, logins and Enrollment included, with `RZ-CP-004`", and add a link to [Sizing and failover](../architecture/04-control-plane-and-gitops.md#sizing-and-failover). The claim then agrees with both sources.

'Ruralz Control's process configuration selects one' states as decided something the owning document still treats as proposed (OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-1 option (a)). The ADR itself proposes adding the Control Store selection to OQ-1. Append "(proposed, OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-1)".

'the only researched library that ships consensus, a pure-Go log store, a network transport and a file snapshot store together' is weak against research section 6: dragonboat also has a built-in transport, snapshotting and Pebble storage. The tech stack document's Alternatives not chosen table rejects dragonboat on S1 ('no release since 2023'). Qualify the claim as 'of the researched libraries that pass S1'. L1-3 gives the same fix.
